Install R for BIGr

Getting Started
Genotype Data
Install R 4.4 or newer, optionally add RStudio Desktop, and verify that BIGr is ready to use.
Keywords

R, installation, RStudio, package setup

What you will install

BIGr requires R 4.4.0 or newer. R is the software that runs the analysis. RStudio Desktop is an optional editor that can make it easier to write scripts, run code, inspect objects, and view plots; it does not replace R and is not required by BIGr.

ImportantInstall R before RStudio

Install R first. If you choose to use RStudio Desktop, install it only after R is working.

1. Install R 4.4 or newer

Choose your operating system and follow the official CRAN instructions.

Operating system Official installer What to choose
Windows Download R for Windows Download the current base installer and accept the standard options.
macOS Download R for macOS Choose the installer that matches Apple silicon or Intel and your macOS version.
Linux R binaries for Linux Open the instructions for your distribution, such as Debian, Fedora, Red Hat, SUSE, or Ubuntu.

When installation finishes, open R itself or a terminal and start R. At the > prompt, run:

R.version.string
getRversion() >= "4.4.0"

A successful check ends with:

[1] TRUE

The version text on the first line will depend on the current R release and your operating system.

WarningIf the result is FALSE

Install a current R release from the CRAN link for your operating system, restart R, and run the check again. BIGr will not install on R versions older than 4.4.0.

2. Optionally install RStudio Desktop

If you want a graphical editor, download RStudio Desktop from Posit. Choose the free open-source RStudio Desktop installer for your operating system.

After installation, open RStudio. Its Console pane should show the R version that it found. Run the same version check there:

getRversion() >= "4.4.0"

RStudio is only an interface. The commands in Software Hub tutorials also work in the standard R console or in an R script run with Rscript.

3. Check basic R commands

Run these commands one line at a time:

2 + 2
mean(c(10, 12, 14))

Expected output:

[1] 4
[1] 12

If both commands work, R can evaluate expressions and create a numeric vector.

4. Install BIGr

BIGr uses packages from both CRAN and Bioconductor. BiocManager configures those repositories and installs the required dependencies. The introductory tutorial also uses ggplot2 to make a plot, so install both packages together.

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}

BiocManager::install(
  c("BIGr", "ggplot2"),
  ask = FALSE,
  update = FALSE
)

Installation requires an internet connection and can take several minutes. You normally run these installation commands only once for each R library.

TipPackage installation is different from loading

BiocManager::install() puts packages on your computer. library(BIGr) loads BIGr into the current R session. You need to load BIGr again whenever you start a new session and want to use it.

5. Verify BIGr and its example data

Restart R, then run:

library(BIGr)

packageVersion("BIGr")

vcf_file <- system.file(
  "iris_DArT_VCF.vcf.gz",
  package = "BIGr"
)

file.exists(vcf_file)
requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)

The package version will depend on when you install BIGr. The final two commands should each return:

[1] TRUE

That result confirms that R can load BIGr and find the VCF file used in the introductory tutorial.

Troubleshooting

RStudio reports an older R version

Close RStudio, install a current R release, and reopen RStudio. If more than one R version is installed, use RStudio’s R version setting to select R 4.4.0 or newer.

A package is unavailable for this version of R

First confirm that getRversion() >= "4.4.0" returns TRUE. Then restart R and run the BIGr installation block again. Copy the complete error message if you need to ask for help; the last line alone often omits the dependency that failed.

A package cannot be updated

Restart R so the package is not in use, then repeat the installation. On a managed computer, you may need help from your system administrator to write to the R library directory.
